(a) Conditions on Use of Test, Assessment, or Screening Tools.—In the case of any test, assessment, or screening tool utilized under the policy on recruitment and enlistment required by subsection (b) of section 532 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1403; 10 U.S.C. 503 note) for the purpose of identifying persons for recruitment and enlistment in the Armed Forces, the Secretary of Defense shall—
        (1) implement a means for ensuring that graduates of a secondary school (as defined in section 9101(38) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7801(38)), including all persons described in subsection (a)(2) of section 532 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012, are required to meet the same standard on the test, assessment, or screening tool; and 
        (2) use uniform testing requirements and grading standards.  
    (b) Rule of Construction.—Nothing in section 532(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 or this section shall be construed to permit the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of a military department to create or use a different grading standard on any test, assessment, or screening tool utilized for the purpose of identifying graduates of a secondary school (as defined in section 9101(38) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7801(38)), including all persons described in subsection (a)(2) of section 532 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012, for recruitment and enlistment in the Armed Forces.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary of Defense to apply the same standards and uniform grading on recruitment tests to all secondary school graduates, and adds a rule of construction barring different grading standards. A tempting reading is that references to "policy" or to secondary school graduates imply outside involvement, but graduates are only the subjects of the testing, not parties consulted on any decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking mandate, or right to sue.
fable.s: (2) use uniform testing requirements and grading standards.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates that the Secretary of Defense implement uniform testing standards for military recruitment. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, states, or experts. The actors involved are federal officials (the Secretary of Defense) and the subjects of the policy (secondary school graduates), but the graduates are not participating in the decision-making process; they are merely subject to the standards. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense shall— (1) implement a means for ensuring that graduates of a secondary school... are required to meet the same standard on the test, assessment, or screening tool; and (2) use uniform testing requirements and grading standards.

opus.w: The section tells the Secretary of Defense to apply uniform testing and grading standards to secondary-school graduates seeking to enlist. No one outside the federal government takes part in that decision: there is no consultation, advisory body, hearing, comment period, rulemaking requirement, or right to sue. Recruits who take the test are like applicants, and the definition excludes applications. Requiring the Secretary to 'implement a means' is an internal management duty, not an outside process.
opus.s:
the Secretary of Defense shall—

opus.b: The tempting misreading is that recruits taking enlistment tests, or the reference to the Defense Department's recruitment "policy," amounts to participation. It doesn't. Taking an enlistment test is like applying for something, which the definition excludes. The section also doesn't call for rulemaking, comment periods, hearings, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates uniform testing standards for military recruitment but does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties in the decision-making process. The involvement of secondary school graduates is limited to taking a test for eligibility, which is an application-like process, not participation in a federal decision. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or consultation with states or tribes mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense shall— (1) implement a means for ensuring that graduates of a secondary school... are required to meet the same standard on the test, assessment, or screening tool; and (2) use uniform testing requirements and grading standards.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section involves "secondary school graduates" (who are outside the federal government), it constitutes participation. However, the text only mandates that these individuals meet uniform testing standards for recruitment. It does not require the government to consult with them, hold hearings for them, or include them in an advisory body. The interaction is purely administrative (testing for eligibility), not participatory in the decision-making process.
